_README: Mission environments. One-way signal delay = distance / speed of light (299,792 km/s), computed at load time in app/config/__init__.py from distance_km (and distance_range_km when the distance varies). The Earth-independent mode rule uses the worst case (distance_km). Distances: NASA NSSDCA planetary fact sheets.

station.name: Low Earth orbit
station.source: Prototype approximation (≈ 1 s, near real-time relay through ground and satellite networks). Not derived from a distance.

lunar_base.name: Lunar base
lunar_base.source: Moon semimajor axis 0.3844 × 10^6 km / 299,792 km/s ≈ 1.28 s. NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/moonfact.html

mars_transit.name: Mars transit
mars_transit.source: Distance from Earth: minimum 54.6 × 10^6 km, maximum 401.4 × 10^6 km; / 299,792 km/s ≈ 182 s to 1,339 s (3 to 22 min). The worst case (maximum) is used. NASA NSSDCA Mars Fact Sheet: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html

autonomy._README: PROTOTYPE DESIGN CHOICES, NOT NASA RULES. Earth-independent mode is active when the overall level is critical AND the round trip (2 x one_way_delay_s) exceeds round_trip_threshold_s. ground_response_s is an assumed time for the flight surgeon to read and answer a report; it is only used to estimate earliest_reply_s and the countdown, never in the rule itself.
